transcript.text: Today we calibrate the main pressure relief valve on manifold B. Check that pump power is isolated and locked out.
First, use a 17 mm open wrench to loosen the locking jam nut by rotating counter-clockwise two full turns.
Why must the hex key remain seated while turning the jam nut?
Holding the 6 mm hex key prevents the internal spring adjuster from spinning and losing our baseline pressure setting. Next, attach the calibrated test gauge to port M3.
Turn the 6 mm hex adjustment screw clockwise until the dial gauge indicates exactly 210 bar.
Finally, re-tighten the 17 mm jam nut to 45 Newton meters torque while holding the hex key stationary.

ground_truth_steps.title: Loosen valve jam nut
ground_truth_steps.instruction: Loosen the 17 mm locking jam nut counter-clockwise two turns while keeping the hex key seated.
ground_truth_steps.success_criteria: Jam nut is backed off two threads; hex adjuster remains in baseline position.
ground_truth_steps.why: Holding the hex key prevents the spring spool from unintentionally shifting baseline pressure.

ground_truth_steps.title: Attach pressure gauge to port M3
ground_truth_steps.instruction: Thread the digital test gauge onto diagnostic test point M3 and hand-tighten.
ground_truth_steps.success_criteria: Test gauge hose coupler is locked onto quick-disconnect port M3 with zero oil seepage.
ground_truth_steps.why: Port M3 measures system pressure directly downstream of the relief valve seat.

ground_truth_steps.title: Adjust relief pressure to 210 bar
ground_truth_steps.instruction: Rotate the 6 mm hex adjustment screw clockwise until gauge reads 210 bar.
ground_truth_steps.success_criteria: Digital gauge displays 210 bar +/- 2 bar steady reading.
ground_truth_steps.why: 210 bar matches factory hydraulic circuit safety rating; exceeding it triggers rupture disc.

ground_truth_steps.title: Torque lock nut to 45 Nm
ground_truth_steps.instruction: Torque the 17 mm lock nut to 45 Nm while maintaining hex key position.
ground_truth_steps.success_criteria: Torque wrench clicks at 45 Nm; adjustment screw has not rotated.
ground_truth_steps.why: Vibration during hydraulic cycling can loosen non-torqued nuts causing pressure drift.
